title: Modified query useProducts to keep the catalogue for five minutes
context: The app requested the catalogue again each time a shopper came back to it more than 30 seconds after it loaded. The app now keeps a loaded catalogue for five minutes, so a shopper who looks at the cart and comes back sees the same products with no new request. A change to a product on the server can now take five minutes to show in the catalogue, where it took 30 seconds before.
- **When** a shopper opens the catalogue for the first time, **then** nothing changes: the page shows "Loading the catalogue…" and then the products.

- **When** a shopper leaves the catalogue and comes back between 30 seconds and five minutes after it loaded, **then** [the page shows the stored products and the app sends no request to `/products`](code:src/hooks/use-products.ts#L9). The app sent a request before.

- **When** a shopper leaves the browser tab and comes back to the catalogue within five minutes of the load, **then** [the app sends no request to `/products`](code:src/hooks/use-products.ts#L9). The app sent a request after 30 seconds before.
- **When** a shopper comes back to the catalogue more than five minutes after it loaded, **then** nothing changes: the app requests `/products` again.
- **When** a shopper opens the account page, **then** nothing changes: the profile is still requested again after 30 seconds.

- Added [`PRODUCTS_STALE_TIME_MS`](code:src/hooks/use-products.ts#PRODUCTS_STALE_TIME_MS), a constant of the module that [holds `300_000`](code:src/hooks/use-products.ts#L6), the number of milliseconds in five minutes. The module does not export it.

- Modified [`useProducts()`](code:src/hooks/use-products.ts#useProducts) to [pass `staleTime: PRODUCTS_STALE_TIME_MS` to `useQuery`](code:src/hooks/use-products.ts#L9). The query had no `staleTime` of its own before, and took the `30_000` that `queryClient` in `src/lib/query-client.ts` sets for every query.
diff: -  return useQuery({ queryKey: PRODUCTS_QUERY_KEY, queryFn: fetchProducts })
+  return useQuery({ queryKey: PRODUCTS_QUERY_KEY, queryFn: fetchProducts, staleTime: PRODUCTS_STALE_TIME_MS })

nodes.label: Holds the stale time of the products query
nodes.description: **The change.** A new constant of the module that [holds `300_000`](code:src/hooks/use-products.ts#L6), the number of milliseconds in five minutes. [`useProducts()` passes it to `useQuery` as `staleTime`](code:src/hooks/use-products.ts#L9), and nothing else reads it. The value has a name so that the options of the query say what the number is.

nodes.label: Runs the products query with a stale time of five minutes
nodes.description: **The change.** `useProducts()` [passes `staleTime: PRODUCTS_STALE_TIME_MS` to `useQuery`](code:src/hooks/use-products.ts#L9), with the same `queryKey` and `queryFn` as before. The query took the `30_000` of `queryClient` in `src/lib/query-client.ts` before. React Query does not call `fetchProducts` again while the stored products are less than 300000 ms old, so a shopper who comes back to the catalogue in that time causes no request to `/products`.

It is on the path because it is the only caller of [`useProducts()`](code:src/hooks/use-products.ts#useProducts): each visit to `/` mounts it, and the mount is when React Query decides to request `/products` or to use the stored products.

nodes.label: The stale time of the products query

contract.now: Not exported from `src/hooks/use-products.ts`. A number, `300_000`, in milliseconds. Only [`useProducts()`](code:src/hooks/use-products.ts#L9) reads it.

nodes.label: The query that loads the catalogue

contract.before: Exported from `src/hooks/use-products.ts`. Takes no arguments and returns the result of `useQuery` for the key `["products"]` and `fetchProducts`. The products are stale 30000 ms after a fetch, the `staleTime` that `queryClient` in `src/lib/query-client.ts` sets for every query.
contract.now: The same surface: no arguments, the same key, the same `queryFn` and the same fields on the result. The products are stale 300000 ms after a fetch, so a caller that mounts in that time gets the stored products and causes no request to `/products`.

nodes.label: The page a shopper sees at `/`
nodes.effect: Calls [`useProducts()`](code:src/hooks/use-products.ts#useProducts) with no arguments and reads `data`, `isPending` and `isError`, which are all still there. A mount between 30000 ms and 300000 ms after a fetch now renders the stored products and [causes no request to `/products`](code:src/hooks/use-products.ts#L9).

nodes.label: The route table of the app
nodes.effect: Renders `<CatalogPage />` with no props as the index route of `/`, and `<CatalogPage />` in `src/routes/catalog/index.tsx` still takes none. The longer stale time changes when the page requests `/products`, not what `router` renders.

waypoints.title: Added the constant `PRODUCTS_STALE_TIME_MS` of five minutes
waypoints.reading: The author added a constant `PRODUCTS_STALE_TIME_MS` that holds `300_000`, the number of milliseconds in five minutes. [`useProducts()` passes it to `useQuery` as `staleTime`](code:src/hooks/use-products.ts#L9), so that the products query has a stale time of its own and does not take the `30_000` of `STALE_TIME_MS` in `src/lib/query-client.ts`. The module does not export the constant, and no other code reads it.

waypoints.title: Modified `useProducts()` to pass a stale time to the query
waypoints.reading: The author modified a query in the function `useProducts()` that now treats the stored products as fresh for 300000 ms after a fetch, up from 30000 ms. The options of `useQuery` now carry `staleTime` with the value of [`PRODUCTS_STALE_TIME_MS`](code:src/hooks/use-products.ts#PRODUCTS_STALE_TIME_MS), and the `queryKey` and the `queryFn` are the same as before. `<CatalogPage />` in `src/routes/catalog/index.tsx` is the only caller, so that a shopper who comes back to `/` within five minutes of a fetch gets the stored products and the app sends no request to `/products`. The same five minutes is how long a change to a product on the server can stay out of the catalogue.
waypoints.needsAttention: This is the one place where the pull request changes what runs: the options of `useQuery` now carry a `staleTime` of 300000 ms, and React Query uses it and not the 30000 ms of `queryClient`. The other waypoint declares [`PRODUCTS_STALE_TIME_MS`](code:src/hooks/use-products.ts#PRODUCTS_STALE_TIME_MS), the value this line reads.
